- Overall token throughput dropped ~55% across our hot routes.

Subject: Re: Fwd: Production spike after v3.2.1 rollout — PillarPay urgent escalation

Hannah/Team,

Quick triage findings from the profiler dump and the samples:
- The q4_2-fused quant profile introduces a new packing for KV cache that causes increased decode kernel switches for seq lengths <64; those switches are triggering expensive slow-paths on our current kernel selector.
- We also see top-1 logits rescaling differences vs v3.1.8 leading to a small but material rise in hallucination-prone tokens in a minority of prompts (attached sample diff).
- No evidence of dataset poisoning; this is a numerical interaction between quantized weights and fused operators.

Workarounds:
- Route PillarPay traffic to v3.1.8 (compatible quant profile q4_0) — immediate fix, zero config change for customer.
- Alternatively, disable the q4_2-fused profile in runtime for the customer's pool (requires infra flip).

I'll produce a short technical note summarizing the delta for release & model teams.

Attachments: profiler_summary.md (text, 12 KB), sample_diffs.patch (text, 8 KB)

— Aditya

Allocations and failover options:
- We can push an immediate runtime routing rule to direct PillarPay traffic to v3.1.8 across their dedicated pool. Estimated time: 6 minutes to propagate.
- If PillarPay is on shared pools, we can apply a per-tenant override to bypass q4_2-fused profile; estimated time: 12 minutes.
- I've verified there is no GPU OOM or system-level throttling; queue depth increased due to slower decode kernels (matches Aditya's analysis).

Recommended immediate action: apply per-tenant override -> route to v3.1.8 and pause q4_2-fused for the customer's pools. I'll coordinate the rollout and monitor.

I'll run a canary traffic sample and report p95/p99 within 15m after flip.

— Markus
